title: Wyndham Street North reconstruction and downtown parking policy
subtitle: Payment-in-lieu of parking, Housing Accelerator Fund, CAO objectives, water financial plan, physician recruitment and top employer awards.
overview: The committee recommended rebuilding Wyndham Street North between Carden and Woolwich streets with one traffic lane each way, parallel parking and separated bike paths on both sides, designed to adapt to the seasonal patio program. For St. George's Square, it recommended keeping an offset intersection similar to today's, with operational improvements and separated bike paths. Staff said construction is planned to start in 2026, with a streetscaping workshop in April and a report in June.

The committee also recommended a new payment-in-lieu of off-street parking policy, effective March 1, 2024, which lets downtown developers pay instead of providing some required parking. The policy was recommended {{vote:m8}}, and a related fee-bylaw change was recommended {{vote:m9}}. Staff said the policy is meant to make it easier to convert upper floors into housing.

On consent, the committee recommended releasing the city's physician recruitment contribution without the Chamber of Commerce match, approved the 2024 budget reporting items and the water and wastewater financial plan, and expanded the governance section's mandate to include the Office of the CAO. Staff presented the $21.4 million federal Housing Accelerator Fund award. After the closed session, the mayor reported that Council received legal advice on the Clair-Maltby Secondary Plan Ontario Land Tribunal matter and gave direction to staff.

decisions.item: Wyndham Street North and St. George's Square design
decisions.detail: The committee recommended rebuilding Wyndham Street North with one lane each way, parallel parking and separated one-way bike paths on both sides, and keeping an offset St. George's Square intersection with improvements.
The committee recommended a policy, effective March 1, 2024, allowing developers to pay a fee instead of providing some required parking.
The committee recommended amending Schedule A of the Development Application Fee Bylaw to add the estimated cost of a parking space and a payment-in-lieu application fee.
The committee approved the CAO's 2024 performance objectives from the closed meeting, and the CAO then presented them publicly.
The committee recommended revising its Terms of Reference so the Governance section covers the Office of the CAO, and directed the Clerk to update related governance policies.
The committee recommended transferring the budgeted one-time physician recruitment contribution to the Guelph-Wellington Ontario Health Team without waiting for the Chamber of Commerce contribution.
The committee recommended that Council, as owner of the drinking water system, approve the current six-year financial plan required under Ontario Regulation 453/07.

debate: On parking policy, one delegate representing downtown businesses argued that payments in place of parking reduce the supply customers rely on, and that the money should be held to replace parking and not used for transit. A second delegate, for an active transportation group, argued that more parking induces more driving and that the money should go to transit and active transportation.

Staff said the policy is a new revenue tool, estimated at about $600,000 a year, and is not full cost recovery. Staff said how the money is split would be set through reserve policies and the multi-year budget, and that engagement relied mainly on the earlier downtown parking master plan work. One councillor asked about limited consultation with developers.

A proposal to direct all payments to transit was withdrawn after staff cautioned that the Planning Act limits how these reserve funds can be used. One councillor supported keeping funds for both parking and alternatives, citing future demand from Conestoga College and the GO train.

On Wyndham Street, delegates supporting the staff plan said protected bike lanes improve safety and accessibility, and that the flexible design with seasonal patios is an acceptable compromise. They also asked for accessible parking and loading zones.

The downtown business association delegate said retail is struggling and favoured wider sidewalks and beautification, with angled parking on one side. The delegate also opposed the traffic circle and preferred keeping the existing character of Douglas Street. Councillors said detailed design, streetscaping and construction phasing would be discussed at the April workshop, and several stressed flexibility.
